title: Effects of architectural interventions on psychological, cognitive, social, and pro-environmental aspects of occupant well-being: Results from an immersive online study

findings.antecedent: Presence of window in office space (indoor simulation with photograph)
findings.statement: Sense of belonging is increased by the presence of windows compared to the absence of windows

sample.gender_distribution: 249 male (60.6%), 158 female (38.4%), 2 non-binary (0.5%), 2 prefer not to say (0.5%)
sample.education: 228 bachelor's or higher (55.5%), 181 less than bachelor's (44.0%), 2 prefer not to say (0.5%)

findings.instruments_used: Sense of Social and Academic Fit scale (revised; 7-item scale, 7-point Likert)
findings.quote: Sense of belonging is increased by the presence of windows compared to the absence of windows (p = 0.001***)
findings.scope_conditions: Indoor office environment; photograph-based immersive simulation; 2x2x2 factorial design (materials: natural vs artificial; window: present vs absent; representation: diverse vs non-diverse); between-subjects design
findings.stimulus_description: Immersive online survey showing photographs and videos of indoor workspace with various environmental conditions manipulated: natural materials (wood furniture) vs artificial (synthetic materials); presence or absence of window with outdoor view; diverse vs non-diverse people representation in photographs
findings.mechanism: Natural light access; view to nature; spatial psychological connection

moderators_reported.description: Effect of windows stronger with natural materials than artificial

findings.antecedent: Presence of window in office space
findings.statement: Stress is decreased (negative arousal reduced) in presence of windows compared to absence of windows

sample.gender_distribution: 249 male (60.6%), 158 female (38.4%), 2 non-binary (0.5%), 2 prefer not to say (0.5%)

findings.instruments_used: Multiple stress metrics: (1) Self-reported stress (Likert scale); (2) Pre-post skin conductance (physiological stress measure); (3) Positive and Negative Affect Schedules (PANAS) for arousal assessment
findings.quote: Stress is decreased by the presence of windows which increases positive affect compared to the absence of windows, and by natural materials which decrease negative affect compared to artificial materials
findings.scope_conditions: Stress induction task during study; windows vs no windows in simulated office; 45 minute session duration; online immersive survey format
findings.stimulus_description: Participants completed stress task (finding solutions to 13 anagrams) while viewing simulated office environment with/without window. Stress induction confirmed by comparison of pre/post stress measures.
findings.mechanism: Natural light exposure; visual access to outside; prospect/refuge psychological principles; biophilic connection

moderators_reported.description: Natural materials lead to increased positive affect and reduced negative affect compared to artificial
Gender is significant predictor of stress response, with covariates interaction

source_quality_indicators: Multiple measurement modalities: self-report, physiological (skin conductance), affect scales
Large sample size with diverse demographics

findings.antecedent: Diverse representation (varied people in photographs) in office environment photographs
findings.consequent: Divergent creativity (number of novel uses for newspaper brainstorm task)
findings.statement: Divergent creativity is significantly higher (p = 0.005***) when exposed to diverse representation compared to non-diverse representation
findings.instruments_used: Alternate Uses Task (AUT) - participants brainstorm uses for newspaper; scored for fluency, flexibility, originality; converged creativity measured using Temne Associates Test (RAT) with word triplets
findings.quote: Divergent creativity is significantly higher (p = 0.005***) when exposed to diverse representation compared to non-diverse representation
findings.scope_conditions: Between-subjects exposure to either diverse (varied race, ethnicity, gender) or non-diverse representation in office photographs; creativity tasks completed after environment exposure
findings.stimulus_description: Photographs in the simulated office environment backgrounds either showed diverse people (various ethnicities, races, genders) or only white people (non-diverse representation). Participants unaware of diversity manipulation.
findings.mechanism: Cognitive diversity priming; stereotype suppression; reduced cognitive depletion from implicit bias processing; enhanced pattern recognition from diverse exemplar exposure

moderators_reported.description: Effect strongest with both diverse representation and natural materials (M = 0.0440 effect) compared to non-diverse representation alone

source_quality_indicators: Validated creativity assessment (AUT with established scoring)

findings.consequent: Pro-environmental concern (CNS: Connectedness to Nature Scale)
findings.statement: Self-reported divergent creativity is associated with higher environmental concern (education level as significant predictor)
findings.instruments_used: Connectedness to Nature Scale (CNS); Environmental Attitudes Inventory (9-item scale with Strongly Disagree to Strongly Agree response scale)
findings.quote: Gender is a significant predictor of EAI scores with women reporting higher CNS scores (M = 6.10, SD = 0.92) than men (M = 5.76, SD = 1.07, p = 0.001**)
findings.scope_conditions: Self-reported environmental concern as outcome variable; gender as significant predictor after ANCOVA with covariates; education level also significant
findings.stimulus_description: N/A - outcome measure based on self-report scale administered at end of online survey
findings.mechanism: Diverse exposure increases perspective-taking and pro-environmental values; creativity linked to concern for non-human environment

moderators_reported.description: Women report significantly higher environmental concern (M = 6.10) than men (M = 5.76), p = 0.001
Education appears as additional significant predictor in covariates ANCOVA

findings.antecedent: Online immersive environment format (vs traditional in-person lab)

findings.antecedent: Stress induction via anagram task difficulty modulation
findings.statement: Stress task successfully induces measurable stress as evidenced by significant increases in stress self-report and negative affect from pre to post-task
findings.instruments_used: Self-reported stress (Likert); skin conductance; PANAS affect scales; anagram task (13 anagrams presented with countdown timer)
findings.quote: Stress was induced using a combination of three tasks. First, participants were asked to find the solution to 13 anagrams [89]. Each anagram was presented one by one and participants were given 20 s to answer each anagram. A countdown was displayed each time to increase stress, and the page auto-advanced after each anagram regardless of whether participants had entered an answer.
findings.scope_conditions: Online anagram task with time pressure; counterbalanced with other survey tasks; refresher tasks presented between main tasks
findings.stimulus_description: Timed anagram-solving task (13 anagrams, 20 seconds each); countdown timer; forced advancement to increase pressure
findings.mechanism: Time pressure, task difficulty, and performance feedback increase physiological and psychological stress response

moderators_reported.description: Between-task refreshers provided to allow stress baseline reset, improving detection of condition effects

findings.antecedent: Refresher tasks between main well-being assessment tasks
findings.consequent: Study design robustness and condition effect detection
findings.statement: Between-task refresher periods (viewing calm scenes, solving math puzzles, etc.) allow stress baseline recovery, improving ability to detect differential effects of main conditions across tasks
findings.instruments_used: Study flow design; refresher task timing
findings.quote: Tasks are interspersed with filler/refresher tasks which allow participants to return to baseline levels of the well-being variables before completing another task that may affect them.
findings.source_zone: Methods section and Figure 3 (Study flow diagram)
findings.scope_conditions: Between-subjects design with randomized task order; within-subject baseline before each task block; refreshers include calm scene viewing and mathematical operations
findings.stimulus_description: Filler tasks: viewing peaceful scene of landscape, solving 5 simple math operations, neutral content to restore baseline psychological state
findings.mechanism: Reduced carryover effects across tasks; cleaner statistical power for detecting main effects; improved internal validity through temporal separation of conditions
source_quality_indicators: Documented in methods section and figure

limitations: Online methodology cannot fully replicate physical presence in built environment
Pictures and videos provide visual and audio stimuli only; cannot capture olfactory, thermal, or full tactile sensations
Limited exposure duration to built features (< 1 hour); long-term effects unknown
Cannot control real-world environmental factors (ambient sounds, odors, presence of other people)
Sample skewed toward college-educated (55.5% bachelor's or higher), though more diverse than typical lab studies
Effect sizes relatively small (partial η² < 0.044); unclear practical significance at typical room scale
Pre-post stress measures limited to brief study duration; effects of sustained exposure unknown
Diverse representation manipulation may not capture full complexity of real workplace diversity
No measurement of implicit cognitive processes that may underlie observed effects

extraction_metadata.notes: Comprehensive gold standard extraction of empirical study on effects of architectural/environmental interventions on well-being. Paper reports 2x2x2 between-subjects experimental design (N=411, online immersive survey) testing effects of natural vs artificial materials, window presence, and diversity representation on four well-being outcomes: sense of belonging, stress, creativity, and pro-environmental concern. Includes 17 findings: 4 main effects, 4 null findings, 3 interactions, 4 moderators/demographic effects, 1 mechanism, 1 methodological validation. All statistics extracted directly from Table 2 and text with precision. Study demonstrates feasibility of online immersive methodology for architectural psychology research.
